survey: An orange round wall-style clock stands upright on its rim on a shallow green floor ledge, just in front of a wall with vertical green stripes. The camera looks almost straight at the clock and slightly down, so a thin strip of floor shows. The orange rim is a thick tube of even width all the way round. The white dial sits inside it, nearly circular and facing the viewer. Twelve hour bars and the minute dots are spaced evenly around a center hub. The 12/6 and 3/9 bars are the same distance from the center, which fits a dial facing the camera. The hour and minute hands come out of the hub. The red second hand runs straight through the hub, and its short tail lines up with its long end. The bottom of the rim touches the floor just in front of the line where the wall meets the floor, with a soft contact shadow. The wall stripes are vertical and the floor edge is horizontal, both matching a near-frontal view.
